eli5.text: The text labels next to branching conversation threads now sit in a straight, even column instead of drifting left or right when they contain characters of different widths. ai.summary: Agents expand by default in CLI. `use-send-message.ts` removed `setCollapsedAgents` calls. `agent-branch-item.tsx` replaced `RaisedPill` with text, removed `branchChar`. Scope: CLI only.

eli5.text: When you work with multiple assistants in the command-line tool, each assistant's details now stay visible by default instead of being tucked away. Previously, the tool would automatically hide (collapse) each assistant's section soon after it started working, so you'd have to click to see what it was doing. Now the tool no longer hides them automatically, so you can see each assistant's progress without taking an extra click. ai.title: Remove branching UI from CLI
ai.summary: Removed branching characters and indent logic from CLI components. Simplified message-block.tsx, tool-call-item.tsx, and related files. Internal refactor.

eli5.text: The branching lines and indentation that previously appeared in the command-line interface to show nested conversation threads have been removed, leaving the plain text content behind. You would see simpler, less cluttered messages when using the command-line assistant, as the visual guide lines that indicated sub-conversations are no longer displayed. This change simplifies the codebase under the hood without altering core functionality.

ai.title: Refactor CLI chat hooks into separate modules
ai.summary: Split monolithic logic from `cli/src/chat.tsx` into dedicated hooks: `use-agent-initialization`, `use-auth-state`, `use-chat-input`, `use-terminal-dimensions`, and `use-validation-banner`. This reduces component complexity by isolating state management, terminal dimension calculations, and agent initialization side effects. The change is internal to the CLI package, affecting `cli/src/hooks/` and `cli/src/chat.tsx`. Each new hook encapsulates specific responsibilities, such as handling auth query mutations or calculating input width based on terminal dimensions.

eli5.text: The CLI chat interface was reorganized so that the single large screen file no longer handles everything itself; instead, it calls on smaller helper modules that each focus on one job, like managing login state, handling what you type, watching terminal size, or showing validation warnings. You won't see anything different on screen right away, but the program will now be easier for developers to maintain and extend. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping that went live today.

ai.title: Remove Prompt/Response labels from CLI agent branch items
ai.summary: Removes explicit 'Prompt' and 'Response' text labels from the CLI agent branch view in `cli/src/components/agent-branch-item.tsx`. The prompt text now uses italic attributes directly, simplifying the visual hierarchy. Scope limited to CLI rendering components.

eli5.text: When you run the CLI agent and branch view shows your conversation, the separate 'Prompt' and 'Response' labels have been removed. The prompt text now appears in italics directly, creating a cleaner visual layout. This affects anyone using the CLI agent branch view to review conversation threads.

ai.title: Add reasoning stream support to CLI print mode
ai.summary: Added `printModeReasoningSchema` to `common/src/types/print-mode.ts` and integrated reasoning chunk handling in `npm-app/src/client.ts`. The CLI now renders reasoning text in gray before the main response, stopping the spinner on first reasoning chunk. Stream state tracking moved to instance variables (`streamStarted`, `textStreamStarted`) to manage interleaved reasoning and text output correctly.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question in the command-line interface, you'll now see the assistant's step-by-step thinking appear in gray text above its main reply. This happens live as the thinking occurs, before the final answer is shown. The change adds support for displaying this reasoning stream in the CLI's plain text output mode, so you can watch the assistant 'think through' your request instead of just seeing the final response appear out of nowhere. This is active today for anyone using the CLI in print mode.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.509 aggregates GPT-5 and CLI tool improvements
ai.summary: Version 1.0.509 is a release-bump commit (npm-app/release/package.json: 1.0.508 to 1.0.509) that aggregates the surrounding day's changes across the Freebuff monorepo. Since 1.0.508, this release introduces GPT-5 orchestration support in base2 agents, the task_completed tool for explicit turn ending, read_subtree tool UI and runtime, PLAN agent mode with build buttons, CLI segmented control and hover toggle refactor, scroll acceleration using CODEBUFF_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER, and several CLI tool component and layout improvements. These changes span the cli, common, agents, and sdk packages. This is a release-bump with no direct code changes to user-facing behavior.
ai.evidence: Commit cc00d30e modifies npm-app/release/package.json, changing the version field from 1.0.508 to 1.0.509 (+1/-1), a release-bump commit that aggregates prior day work across the Freebuff monorepo.

eli5.text: This release adds support for the GPT-5 AI model and rolls out a new plan-first workflow mode in the CLI, along with major improvements to code searching, terminal scrolling, and slash-command usability. You can now run the agent in a dedicated PLAN mode that produces a structured plan before building, with clickable 'Build Fast' and 'Build Max' buttons to kick off implementation. Code search got a major upgrade: it now handles tricky file paths correctly, returns surrounding context lines for matches, and stops early instead of hanging on slow or overly broad searches. The terminal interface received a fresh TUI design with raised interactive pills, transparent theme backgrounds that match your terminal colors, and smooth scrolling tuned for popular terminals like Zed, Ghostty, and VS Code. New tools like task_completed and read_subtree give agents cleaner ways to signal completion and scan project structures, while slash commands like /init, /clear, and /new make navigation and session management more intuitive. Upgrading gives you faster, more reliable searches, better visual polish in the terminal, and smarter agent workflows that separate planning from execution.

ai.summary: The Freebuff SDK package version has been incremented from 0.6.1 to 0.7.0 in sdk/package.json. This release consolidates several prior commits addressing CLI tooling improvements, scroll acceleration refinements, agent mode toggle enhancements, and reasoning stream support. Notable changes in this release include the addition of the read_subtree and write_todos tool UI components, the introduction of the DiffViewer for str_replace and write_file outputs, and separate reasoning chunk handling in the CLI print mode. New interactive menus let you pick different agent modes (Fast, Max, Plan) with hover effects, and new tool previews show file searches, directory listings, todo lists, and code diffs right in your terminal. Terminal scrolling speeds are now fine-tuned for different terminal programs like Zed and Ghostty, fixing jumpy or too-slow behavior. A few search and file-handling bugs are fixed, like searching for text that starts with special characters and glob patterns matching files in the wrong folders. Upgrading gives you a cleaner, more responsive chat experience with better visual feedback and fewer glitches when browsing code results.

ai.summary: MessageBlock now checks for `includeToolCall: false` in tool input and returns null. Prevents rendering of specific tool calls in CLI. Affects `cli/src/components/message-block.tsx`. Internal rendering logic change.

eli5.text: When you run a command that would normally print a tool's action to the screen, you can now mark that specific action as hidden, and the assistant will leave it out of what it displays to you. This is done by setting a flag on the tool's input that tells the display logic to skip it, so anything with includeToolCall set to false simply won't appear in the message output. You'd notice this as a way to keep sensitive or noisy tool activity from showing up in your terminal session, and it's active today whenever a tool is invoked with that flag.
